intro: This branch introduces differential equations, which describe how something changes and ask what it will look like over time. They model growth, cooling, populations and mixing.

VI.7.01.what: A differential equation links a quantity to its own rate of change. For example, a population grows faster the bigger it already is.

levels.a: Recognizes an equation that includes a derivative.
levels.b: Identifies the order, the highest derivative that appears.
levels.c: Explains that the solution is a whole function, not a single number.
levels.d: Translates a differential equation into an everyday sentence.

VI.7.02.what: Checking whether a suggested function really solves a differential equation by plugging it in.

levels.b: Substitutes it and its derivative into the equation.
levels.c: Checks that both sides of the equation match.
levels.d: Finds a constant that makes a suggested solution work.

VI.7.03.what: A slope field is a picture made of tiny line segments showing which way solutions flow at every point, like wind arrows on a weather map.

levels.a: Draws short slope marks at points using the equation.
levels.b: Matches slope field pictures to their equations.
levels.c: Sketches a solution curve by following the slopes.
levels.d: Uses lines of equal slope to predict long-run behavior.

VI.7.04.what: Euler's method: estimating a solution by taking small straight steps in the direction the equation points.

levels.a: Explains stepping along the tangent line to a new point.
levels.c: Sees how smaller steps give a better estimate.
levels.d: Decides whether the estimate is too high or too low.

VI.7.05.what: Solving equations where all the y terms can be moved to one side and all the x terms to the other.

levels.a: Moves y terms and x terms to opposite sides.
levels.c: Rearranges to get y on its own.
levels.d: Uses a starting value, and watches for solutions lost when dividing.

VI.7.06.what: Modeling things that grow or shrink at a rate proportional to their size, like savings earning interest or radioactive decay.

levels.a: Recognizes the equation where the rate is a constant times the amount.
levels.b: Writes its solution as a starting amount times an exponential.
levels.c: Finds the growth constant from data, like a half-life.
levels.d: Uses the model to make predictions.

VI.7.07.what: Newton's law of cooling: a hot drink cools faster when it is much hotter than the room, and slower as it nears room temperature.

levels.c: Finds the cooling constant from measurements.
levels.d: Works backwards to find when cooling began, as in detective problems.

VI.7.08.what: Logistic growth models a population that grows quickly at first, then levels off as it nears the most its environment can support.

levels.a: Explains the carrying capacity, the population ceiling.
levels.c: Shows growth is fastest at half the carrying capacity.
levels.d: Solves it, reads off its features, and adds removal like fishing.

VI.7.09.what: A differential equation has a whole family of solutions. One known starting value picks out the specific one.

levels.a: Describes the family of all solutions.
levels.b: Uses a starting value to pick one solution from the family.
levels.c: Spots unusual solutions that the general formula misses.
levels.d: Graphs several members of the family together.

VI.7.10.what: Modeling a tank where salty water flows in and mixed water flows out, to track how much salt is inside.

levels.a: Writes the change as rate in minus rate out.
levels.b: Sets up the equation for the tank.
levels.d: Finds the amount the tank settles toward in the long run.

VI.7.11.what: Finding steady states where nothing changes, and whether things drift back to them or run away if nudged.

levels.a: Finds equilibrium values, where the rate of change is zero.
levels.b: Draws a phase line showing which way values move.
levels.c: Classifies each equilibrium as stable or unstable.
levels.d: Studies how equilibria appear or vanish as a setting changes.

VI.7.12.what: Turning a description in words into a differential equation, and checking it makes sense.

levels.a: Translates "proportional to" into a constant times a quantity.
levels.b: Writes the full equation from a word description.
levels.c: States the assumptions the model makes.
levels.d: Checks that the units on both sides match.
